title: api-gateway: adjust streaming proxy buffers, routing rules, and payload limits to stabilize tool-calling and OpenAI-compat surface
author: Maya Chen
description: Motivation: Recent incidents and customer reports surfaced intermittent streaming stalls and malformed tool/function-calling payloads when requests traverse the API gateway proxy under head-of-line pressure. This PR tightens routing rules, increases streaming proxy buffer thresholds for in-flight tool call frames, and enforces conservative request/response payload size limits for OpenAI-compat endpoints to prevent silent truncation. Changes are targeted to avoid behavior changes for most customers while stopping edge-case stalls and improving observability. Approach: 1) Routing: introduce a capacity-aware routing decision that prefers local model variants for short-lived streaming sessions and only falls back to cross-region replicas when local buffer pools exceed 80% usage. 2) Streaming proxy buffers: increase per-connection buffer cap from 128KB to 512KB for tool/function-call frames and add an explicit per-message sanity check to reject oversized tool payloads with a descriptive 413-like error for OpenAI-compat requests. 3) Payload limits: set a soft request/response body limit of 1.5MB for OpenAI-compat chat completion endpoints and add explicit reason codes in gateway logs for truncation/rejection. 4) Graceful fallback: when buffer pressure is high we now proactively downgrade to chunked-mode stream that sends proxy-level keepalive noop frames to prevent stalls. 5) Observability and CI: add metrics for "gateway.buffer_utilization", "gateway.toolframe_drops", and tracing tags for routing_decision. Testing: unit tests for routing decision logic, integration tests exercising streaming with simulated slow clients, and an end-to-end canary that validated tool-calling with sample function schemas. Rollout: feature-flag gated; enabling default after 72h successful canary and one-week gradual rollout. This PR includes minor OpenAI-compat surface tweaks to return the new 413-like error string and machine-readable reason in the compatibility layer. Related: ENG-2045, PM-112. For details see the commit list and changed files below.
commits: refactor(gateway): extract buffer pool abstraction and expose utilization metrics
feat(gateway): capacity-aware routing decision with fallback to chunked-mode streaming
fix(gateway): increase per-connection streaming buffer cap for tool frames and add per-message size checks
chore(test): add integration test that simulates slow client streaming tool calls
docs(api): document OpenAI-compat 413-like response and reason_code for oversized tool payloads
ci: add flaky test retry for streaming integration
review_comments: Arjun: Can we make the 80% threshold configurable via config and feature flag? Author: done - added gateway.buffer_routing_threshold to defaults and feature flag (ff.gateway.capacity_routing).

Lena: The 1.5MB soft limit is a little aggressive for some multimodal flows; can we surface this as a soft limit with a warning header instead of hard reject? Author: kept hard reject for OpenAI-compat tool payloads but added a warning header for non-compat endpoints; added docs and a migration note.
Oliver: Add more telemetry around reason_code so SRE can triage incidents faster. Author: added gateway.toolframe_drops and routing_decision tags to traces.
release_notes: Stabilize streaming and tool/function-calling through gateway-level buffer and routing improvements. OpenAI-compat endpoints gain explicit oversize payload rejection with a 413-like response and machine-readable reason_code. Metrics added: gateway.buffer_utilization, gateway.toolframe_drops.
